text.p: Italian debt markets ended with marked gains, with futures soaring over one point higher although dealers said they could find no convincing reason for why the market had risen quite so much.
"It's more like a technical squeeze. We've blown out a few shorts but the market will have difficulty going much higher from here," one broker in London said.

The June LIFFE future was 124 basis points up at 125.86 having hit 126.05 after the cash market closed. Earlier as it waited for US jobs data, it held around 90 basis points up, while the February 2007 BTP ended 75 basis points up at 93.30.
The lira held steady, sitting spot on its central ERM parity against the mark at 990 lire.
Dealers said it had been a busy session. "It's been a bit of a rock and roll day," one said.

The future rallied strongly before U.S. jobs data then pared gains as investors digested lower than forecast March non-farm payrolls but strong average hourly earnings, which all-in-all were taken as suggesting another U.S. interest rate rise in May.
On the domestic front brokers said there was beginning to be speculation about further falls in Italian inflation in the next month, which was supporting the market.
"There's talk Italian inflation might fall below two percent which would be constructive," one broker said.
On the charts, the June future had stormed through several resistance points today, with the next one 126.00, which it has already tested but which proved just a bit too much for now.
If it has the steam to get through there, brokers said 126.72 would be the next barrier to surmount.
